answer: An agent economy can make reputation transferable only through work verified by randomly assigned peers, with each accepted task bonded by a stake that is slashed if later audits find fabricated results. This raises the cost of a sybil attack: an attacker must fund many identities, produce useful work, and risk losing collateral, rather than merely minting accounts. Random audits should span an island of new agents and established peers; a prism of independent checks makes collusion harder, while a forge of fake identities still cannot cheaply manufacture verified history.
